questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (genus) with List-II (common name) and choose the correct option.
List-I
(a) Aptenodytes
(b) Neophron
(c) Pteropus
(d) Balaenoptera
List-II
(i) Flying fox
(ii) Blue whale
(iii) Penguin
(iv) Vulture
questions.explanation:
(a) Aptenodytes is the penguin, a flightless bird, so (a)-(iii).
(b) Neophron is the vulture, so (b)-(iv).
(c) Pteropus is the flying fox. It is a mammal (a bat), not a bird, even though it flies. So (c)-(i).
(d) Balaenoptera is the blue whale, so (d)-(ii).
Only option (1) gives this combination.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Digestion in cnidarians is both extracellular and intracellular.
Reason (R): Cnidarians exhibit cellular level of organisation, like sponges.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: cnidarians digest food extracellularly in the gastro-vascular cavity, and then intracellularly inside cells lining it.
R is false: cnidarians show tissue level of organisation. The cellular level (loose aggregates of cells) is seen in sponges.
Since R is false, options (1) and (2) cannot apply.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Sponges consist of loose aggregates of cells with only some division of labour among them. Which level of organisation do they show?
questions.explanation:
Key fact: Sponges are multicellular, but their cells are not organised into true tissues.
The cells form loose aggregates with only a little division of labour. This is the cellular level of organisation.
Why not tissue level: True tissues first appear in coelenterates (cnidarians), not in sponges. Organ and organ-system levels appear even later.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In coelenterates, the cnidoblasts (cnidocytes) found on the tentacles and body are mainly used for:
options: Locomotion through rows of beating cilia
Anchorage, defence and capture of prey
Secretion of the calcium carbonate skeleton in all members
questions.explanation:
Cnidoblasts (cnidocytes) contain stinging capsules called nematocysts. They are present on the tentacles and body.
They are used for anchorage, defence and capture of prey. The phylum name Cnidaria comes from these cells.
Option (1) is tempting but wrong: locomotion by rows of ciliated comb plates is a feature of ctenophores.
Options (3) and (4) are not functions of cnidoblasts.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following statements is incorrect?
options: In cockroaches and prawns excretion of waste material occurs through malpighian tubules.
In ctenophores, locomotion is mediated by comb plates.
In Fasciola, flame cells help in excretion
Earthworms are hermaphrodites and yet cross fertilization take place among them.
questions.explanation:
(1) Incorrect: Cockroaches excrete through Malpighian tubules, but prawns excrete through green (antennal) glands.
(2) Correct: Ctenophores swim using eight rows of ciliated comb plates.
(3) Correct: Fasciola, a platyhelminth, uses flame cells for excretion and osmoregulation.
(4) Correct: Earthworms are hermaphrodites, yet they show cross-fertilisation.
Answer: (1)
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 4 (MCQ Q8)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Both echinoderms and hemichordates are triploblastic, coelomate animals with an organ-system level of organisation and a complete digestive system.
Statement II: Like chordates, hemichordates possess a closed circulatory system.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct: echinoderms and hemichordates are both triploblastic, coelomate animals with an organ-system level of organisation and a complete digestive system.
Statement II is incorrect: hemichordates have an open circulatory system, unlike the closed system of chordates.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The stinging capsules called nematocysts are found inside which cells of coelenterates?
questions.explanation:
Key fact: cnidarians have cnidoblasts (cnidocytes) on the tentacles and body. These cells contain stinging capsules called nematocysts.
Nematocysts are used for anchorage, defence and capturing prey. The phylum name Cnidaria comes from these cells.
Choanocytes are the collar cells of sponges. Flame cells are excretory cells of flatworms. Nephridia are excretory organs of annelids.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In birds, the skin is dry. Which is the only gland present in it?
options: Oil gland at the base of the tail
Sebaceous gland at the base of each feather
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: bird skin is dry and has no glands except the oil (preen) gland at the base of the tail.
The birds use its oily secretion to waterproof their feathers, so option (2) fits.
Sweat glands and sebaceous glands are features of mammalian skin, not bird skin. This rules out (1) and (4).
Birds have no mucous glands around the beak, so (3) is also wrong.
Answer: (2)

questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
A. Bombyx
B. Laccifer
C. Limulus
D. Locusta
List-II
I. Living fossil
II. Gregarious pest
III. Silkworm
IV. Lac insect
questions.explanation:
A. Bombyx is the silkworm, so A-III.
B. Laccifer is the lac insect, so B-IV.
C. Limulus (king crab) is a living fossil, so C-I.
D. Locusta is a gregarious pest, so D-II.
Only option (1) gives this combination.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following animals have an open type of circulatory system?
Locusta, Balanoglossus, Pheretima, Branchiostoma, Petromyzon, Limulus, Ascaris
questions.explanation:
Open circulation: Locusta and Limulus (both arthropods), and Balanoglossus (hemichordates have an open circulatory system).
Closed circulation: Pheretima (annelid), Branchiostoma and Petromyzon (chordates).
Ascaris (an aschelminth) has no circulatory system at all.
Count = 3.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct?
options: All reptiles have a three-chambered heart, as all amphibians do
Hyla and Salamandra show internal fertilisation and direct development
Chelone and Testudo have dry cornified skin and cannot regulate their body temperature
Ichthyophis, being limbless, is placed in class Reptilia along with snakes
questions.explanation:
(1) Wrong: crocodiles are reptiles but have a four-chambered heart.
(2) Wrong: Hyla and Salamandra are amphibians, so they show external fertilisation and indirect development.
(3) Correct: turtles (Chelone) and tortoises (Testudo) are reptiles, with dry cornified skin. They are poikilothermous, meaning they cannot regulate body temperature.
(4) Wrong: Ichthyophis is a limbless amphibian, not a reptile.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Mesoglea is present in between ectoderm and endoderm in Obelia.
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: Obelia is a cnidarian, and its mesoglea lies between the ectoderm and endoderm.
(2) Correct: Adult Asterias (starfish), like other adult echinoderms, shows radial symmetry.
(3) Incorrect: Fasciola (liver fluke) is a platyhelminth. Flatworms are acoelomate, not pseudocoelomate.
(4) Correct: Taenia (tapeworm) is a flatworm, and flatworms are triploblastic.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (excretory/osmoregulatory structure) with List-II (phylum).
List-I
(A) Flame cells
(B) Malpighian tubules
(C) Proboscis gland
(D) Nephridia
List-II
(i) Hemichordata
(ii) Annelida
(iii) Platyhelminthes
(iv) Arthropoda
questions.explanation:
(A) Flame cells are the excretory cells of Platyhelminthes, so A matches (iii).
(B) Malpighian tubules are the excretory organs of Arthropoda, so B matches (iv).
(C) The proboscis gland is the excretory organ of Hemichordata, so C matches (i).
(D) Nephridia help in osmoregulation and excretion in Annelida, so D matches (ii).
The matching set is A-(iii), B-(iv), C-(i), D-(ii).
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following cartilaginous fishes possesses electric organs?
questions.explanation:
NCERT lists Torpedo (electric ray) as the cartilaginous fish with electric organs.
Trygon is the tempting wrong option. It is the sting ray and has a poison sting, not electric organs.
Pristis is the saw fish and Scoliodon is the dog fish. Neither has electric organs.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which pair consists of two triploblastic, bilaterally symmetrical animals in which the first is acoelomate and the second is pseudocoelomate?
questions.explanation:
Taenia (tapeworm) is a triploblastic, bilateral flatworm with no body cavity, so it is acoelomate.
Wuchereria (filarial worm) is a roundworm with a pseudocoelom.
So option (3) gives the required acoelomate–pseudocoelomate order.
Fasciola and Planaria are both acoelomate.
Ascaris and Ancylostoma are both pseudocoelomate.
Pheretima is a true coelomate.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which feature is shared by Pheretima and Locusta but is absent in Ascaris?
options: A true body cavity lined by mesoderm
questions.explanation:
Pheretima (an annelid) and Locusta (an arthropod) are both true coelomates. Their body cavity is lined by mesoderm.
Ascaris is a pseudocoelomate, so it lacks a true coelom. That makes option (4) the shared feature absent in Ascaris.
Option (1) fails because closed circulation is found only in Pheretima.
Option (2) fails because malpighian tubules are found only in Locusta.
Option (3) fails because Ascaris also has a complete alimentary canal.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (structure in sponges) with List-II (role):
List-I
A. Ostia
B. Osculum
C. Spongocoel
D. Spicules
List-II
I. Central cavity receiving water
II. Support of the body
III. Minute pores for water entry
IV. Opening through which water exits
questions.explanation:
A. Ostia are minute pores through which water enters the body → III.
B. Osculum is the opening through which water leaves → IV.
C. Spongocoel is the central cavity that receives water from the canals → I.
D. Spicules, along with spongin fibres, form the skeleton that supports the body → II.
So the matching is A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Fertilisation in frogs is external.
Reason (R): Amphibians are oviparous and their development is direct.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: frogs, like other amphibians, release eggs and sperm into water, so fertilisation is external.
R is false: amphibians are oviparous, but their development is indirect. The egg hatches into a tadpole larva that undergoes metamorphosis into the adult.
Direct development, with no larval stage, is a feature of reptiles.
So A is true and R is false.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A marine colonial cnidarian shows a sessile, cylindrical stage that gives rise to umbrella-shaped, free-swimming individuals. These free-swimming individuals in turn give rise to the sessile stage again. Identify the free-swimming form and the mode by which it produces the sessile stage.
questions.explanation:
The sessile, cylindrical form is the polyp. The umbrella-shaped, free-swimming form is the medusa.
In metagenesis (e.g. Obelia), polyps produce medusae asexually by budding.
Medusae form gametes, and the resulting zygote develops into a polyp, so medusae produce polyps sexually.
The trap is option (2), which reverses the two modes.
Answer: (1)

questions.question:
Match List-I (genus) with List-II (common name).
List-I:
A. Physalia
B. Pennatula
C. Gorgonia
D. Meandrina
List-II:
I. Sea-fan
II. Brain coral
III. Portuguese man-of-war
IV. Sea-pen
Choose the correct option.

A. Physalia = Portuguese man-of-war (III).
B. Pennatula = sea-pen (IV).
C. Gorgonia = sea-fan (I).
D. Meandrina = brain coral (II).

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about ctenophores is incorrect?
options: They bear eight external rows of ciliated comb plates for locomotion
Sexes are separate and fertilisation is internal
They reproduce only by sexual means
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: ctenophores have eight external rows of ciliated comb plates for locomotion.
(2) Correct: bioluminescence is well-marked.
(3) Incorrect: sexes are not separate, since they are hermaphrodite. Fertilisation is external and development is indirect.
(4) Correct: reproduction takes place only by sexual means.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In which of the following chordates does the notochord extend from the head to the tail region and persist throughout life?
questions.explanation:
According to NCERT, the notochord in Cephalochordata extends from head to tail and persists throughout life. Branchiostoma (Amphioxus) is the example.
Ascidia, Salpa and Doliolum are all urochordates. In them the notochord is present only in the larval tail and does not last into adult life.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The file-like rasping organ in the mouth of molluscs, used for feeding, is called the:
questions.explanation:
Key fact: the mouth of a mollusc contains a file-like rasping organ called the radula, which is used to scrape food.
The mantle is the soft, spongy skin fold covering the visceral hump, so it is not used for feeding.
The osculum is the water outlet of sponges.
The proboscis is the anterior body region of hemichordates.
Answer: (1)

questions.question: Which of the following genera is correctly matched with its common name?
questions.explanation:

(1) Wrong: Wuchereria is the filaria worm.
(2) Wrong: Fasciola is the liver fluke.
(3) Correct: Ancylostoma is the hookworm.
(4) Wrong: Taenia is the tapeworm.
Only option (3) is correctly matched.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Development in sponges is described as indirect.
Reason (R): Sponges pass through a larval stage that is morphologically distinct from the adult.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. NCERT states that development in sponges is indirect.
R is true. Sponges have a larval stage that is morphologically distinct from the adult.
Indirect development is defined by passing through such a distinct larval stage. So R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which group of animals is mostly asymmetrical, meaning that no plane passing through the centre divides the body into equal halves?
questions.explanation:
An asymmetrical animal cannot be divided into equal halves by any plane through the centre.
NCERT cites sponges (Porifera) as mostly asymmetrical.
Coelenterates and ctenophores are radially symmetrical.
Flatworms are bilaterally symmetrical.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (genus) with List-II (common name):
List-I: (a) Pinctada (b) Antedon (c) Gorgonia (d) Myxine
List-II: (i) Sea-fan (ii) Hagfish (iii) Pearl oyster (iv) Sea lily
questions.explanation:
(a) Pinctada is the pearl oyster, a mollusc: a-iii.
(b) Antedon is the sea lily, an echinoderm, not a plant or cnidarian: b-iv.
(c) Gorgonia is the sea-fan, a cnidarian: c-i.
(d) Myxine is the hagfish, a cyclostome: d-ii.
The pairing a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii matches option 1.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Based on the broad classification of Kingdom Animalia, which one of the following generalisations is correct?
options: Every radially symmetrical animal is diploblastic
Every triploblastic animal possesses a true coelom
Every chordate retains its notochord throughout life
Every animal with organ-system level of organisation is triploblastic
questions.explanation:
(1) False. Adult echinoderms are radially symmetrical but triploblastic.
(2) False. Flatworms are acoelomate and roundworms are pseudocoelomate, yet both are triploblastic.
(3) False. In vertebrates the notochord is replaced by the vertebral column, and in urochordates it is present only in the larva.
(4) True. Organ-system organisation begins with Aschelminthes, and every phylum from there onwards is triploblastic.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: In Pheretima, the body is divided externally and internally into segments with serial repetition of at least some organs.
Statement II: The neural system of annelids consists of paired ganglia connected by lateral nerves to a single dorsal hollow nerve cord.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. Pheretima shows metamerism: the body is segmented externally and internally, with serial repetition of some organs.
Statement II is incorrect. In annelids, paired ganglia are connected by lateral nerves to a double ventral nerve cord. A single dorsal hollow nerve cord is a chordate feature.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (body organisation feature) with List-II (example animal).
List-I
A. Body cavity lined by mesoderm
B. Mesoderm present as scattered pouches between ectoderm and endoderm
C. Body cavity absent
D. Undifferentiated mesoglea between ectoderm and endoderm
List-II
I. Ascaris
II. Taenia
III. Pheretima
IV. Adamsia
Choose the correct answer:
questions.explanation:
A. A body cavity lined by mesoderm is a true coelom, as in Pheretima. So A-III.
B. Mesoderm present as scattered pouches gives a pseudocoelom, as in Ascaris. So B-I.
C. No body cavity means an acoelomate, as in the flatworm Taenia. So C-II.
D. Undifferentiated mesoglea between ectoderm and endoderm marks a diploblastic coelenterate, Adamsia. So D-IV.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In amphibians, the alimentary canal, urinary tract and reproductive tract open into a common chamber that opens to the exterior. This chamber is called:
questions.explanation:
In amphibians, the alimentary canal, urinary tract and reproductive tract all open into one common chamber called the cloaca, which opens to the outside.
The mantle cavity is found in molluscs.
The pseudocoelom is the body cavity of Aschelminthes.
The spongocoel is the central cavity of sponges.
So only 'cloaca' fits the description.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: In Urochordata, the notochord is present only in the larval tail.
Statement II: In Cephalochordata, the notochord is replaced by a cartilaginous vertebral column in the adult.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. In Urochordata (e.g., Ascidia), the notochord is present only in the larval tail.
Statement II is incorrect. In Cephalochordata (e.g., Branchiostoma), the notochord runs from head to tail and persists throughout life.
Replacement of the notochord by a vertebral column happens only in vertebrates.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) Bony fishes have four pairs of gills, each side covered by an operculum.
(ii) Labeo and Catla have skin covered with placoid scales.
(iii) In male Scoliodon, the pelvic fins bear claspers.
(iv) Cyclostomes are freshwater animals that migrate to the sea for spawning.
(v) Teeth of cartilaginous fishes are modified placoid scales that are backwardly directed.
(vi) Osteichthyes mostly show internal fertilisation and viviparity.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: bony fishes have four pairs of gills, covered by an operculum on each side.
(ii) Incorrect: Labeo and Catla are bony fishes with cycloid/ctenoid scales, not placoid scales.
(iii) Correct: in males, the pelvic fins bear claspers.
(iv) Incorrect: cyclostomes are marine and migrate to fresh water to spawn.
(v) Correct: the teeth of cartilaginous fishes are modified, backwardly directed placoid scales.
(vi) Incorrect: bony fishes mostly show external fertilisation and are mostly oviparous.
So three statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: In Platyhelminthes, the digestive system is called incomplete because a single opening to the outside serves as both mouth and anus.
Statement II: In arthropods, blood is circulated through a series of vessels of varying diameters (arteries, veins and capillaries), so their circulatory system is of the closed type.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. Flatworms have a single opening that acts as both mouth and anus, so their digestive system is incomplete.
Statement II is incorrect. Arthropods have an open circulatory system, in which the pumped blood directly bathes cells and tissues. A closed system of arteries, veins and capillaries is found in annelids and chordates.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are true for phylum Echinodermata?
(a) All members are marine.
(b) An excretory system is absent.
(c) Adults are bilaterally symmetrical while larvae are radially symmetrical.
(d) Fertilisation is usually external.
(e) The mouth is on the dorsal side and the anus on the ventral side.
(f) Sexes are separate.
(g) Development is indirect with a free-swimming larva.
questions.explanation:
(a) True: all echinoderms are marine.
(b) True: they have no excretory system.
(c) False: it is reversed, since adults are radial and larvae are bilateral.
(d) True: fertilisation is usually external.
(e) False: the mouth is ventral and the anus is dorsal.
(f) True: sexes are separate.
(g) True: development is indirect with a free-swimming larva.
That makes five true statements.
Answer: (3)

questions.question: Which cartilaginous fish possesses electric organs?
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: some cartilaginous fishes have electric organs, for example Torpedo (electric ray).
Others have a poison sting, for example Trygon (sting ray). This is the most common mix-up.
Pristis is the saw fish and Carcharodon is the great white shark. Neither has electric organs.

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following sets of animals share a four chambered heart?
questions.explanation:
Key fact (NCERT): Most reptiles have an incompletely divided ventricle, giving a three-chambered heart. Crocodiles are the exception and have four chambers.
Birds and mammals both have a four-chambered heart.
So crocodiles, birds and mammals all share a four-chambered heart.
Option (1) fails because amphibians have three chambers.
Options (3) and (4) fail because lizards and turtles have three chambers.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Limulus, the king crab, is often called a 'living fossil'. To which phylum does it belong?
questions.explanation:
Key fact: NCERT names Limulus (king crab) as a living fossil and places it in phylum Arthropoda.
It has jointed appendages and a chitinous exoskeleton, which are arthropod features.
Despite its name, it is not a true crab. Its nearest relatives are spiders and scorpions.
It has no mantle or shell-secreting body plan, so it is not a mollusc. It also lacks a water vascular system and pentamerous symmetry, so it is not an echinoderm.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match the excretory or osmoregulatory structure in List-I with the phylum in List-II.
List-I
A. Flame cells
B. Nephridia
C. Malpighian tubules
D. Proboscis gland
List-II
I. Hemichordata
II. Arthropoda
III. Platyhelminthes
IV. Annelida
questions.explanation:
A. Flame cells are found in Platyhelminthes (III).
B. Nephridia are found in Annelida (IV). Do not assign them to flatworms.
C. Malpighian tubules are found in Arthropoda (II).
D. The proboscis gland is found in Hemichordata (I).
So the correct match is A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A worm-like marine animal has a cylindrical body made of a proboscis, a collar and a trunk. It has a rudimentary notochord-like structure in the collar region, an open circulatory system and a proboscis gland. Which statement about this animal is correct?
options: It belongs to a subphylum of Chordata because it possesses a stomochord
It is a triploblastic coelomate non-chordate with external fertilisation and indirect development
It is a pseudocoelomate with a closed circulatory system like vertebrates
Its stomochord is a true notochord that is replaced by a vertebral column in the adult
questions.explanation:
A body divided into proboscis, collar and trunk, with a stomochord, open circulation and a proboscis gland, identifies a hemichordate such as Balanoglossus.
Hemichordates are now a separate non-chordate phylum. They are triploblastic and coelomate, with external fertilisation and indirect development, so option 2 is correct.
Option 1 fails because the stomochord only resembles a notochord; this was the old reason for placing them under Chordata.
Option 3 fails because they are coelomates with open circulation.
Option 4 fails because the stomochord is not a true notochord and no vertebral column forms.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Sponges are described as mostly asymmetrical animals.
Reason (R): In sponges, any plane passing through the centre of the body divides it into two equal halves.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Sponges are mostly asymmetrical.
R is false. Asymmetry means that no plane through the centre divides the body into equal halves.
R describes the opposite situation, the case where any plane gives equal halves.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(a) Teeth of Chondrichthyes are modified placoid scales directed backwards.
(b) Osteichthyes have four pairs of gills covered by an operculum on each side.
(c) Reptiles possess external ear openings in addition to a tympanum.
(d) The skin of birds is dry and lacks glands except the oil gland at the base of the tail.
(e) The heart of crocodiles is three-chambered like that of other reptiles.
Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation:
(a) Correct: In Chondrichthyes, teeth are modified placoid scales directed backwards.
(b) Correct: Bony fishes have four pairs of gills covered by an operculum on each side.
(c) Incorrect: Reptiles lack external ear openings. The tympanum represents the ear.
(d) Correct: Bird skin is dry and has no glands except the oil gland at the base of the tail.
(e) Incorrect: Crocodiles are the exception among reptiles, with a four-chambered heart.
So (a), (b) and (d) are correct.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The heart of an amphibian such as Rana consists of:
questions.explanation:
Amphibians such as Rana have a three-chambered heart, with two auricles and one ventricle.
One auricle and one ventricle is the two-chambered heart of fishes.
Two auricles and two ventricles is the four-chambered heart of crocodiles, birds and mammals.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (genus) with List-II (common name).
List-I: (A) Struthio (B) Aptenodytes (C) Neophron (D) Columba
List-II: (I) Vulture (II) Pigeon (III) Ostrich (IV) Penguin
questions.explanation:
Struthio is the ostrich, so A-III.
Aptenodytes is the penguin, so B-IV.
Neophron is the vulture, so C-I.
Columba is the pigeon, so D-II.
This gives A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II, which is option (1).
Take care not to swap the two flightless birds, Struthio and Aptenodytes.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Some parasitic flatworms, such as Taenia, absorb nutrients from the host directly through their body surface.
Statement II: In Aschelminthes, development is always indirect, so the young never resemble the adult.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. NCERT notes that some parasitic flatworms, such as Taenia, absorb nutrients from the host directly through their body surface.
Statement II is incorrect. In Aschelminthes, development may be direct, where the young resemble the adult. It may also be indirect, with a larval stage. So development is not always indirect.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) Ctenophores reproduce both sexually and asexually.
(ii) In Obelia, medusae give rise to polyps by sexual reproduction.
(iii) Digestion in cnidarians is both extracellular and intracellular.
(iv) Fertilisation in ctenophores is internal.
(v) Corals have a skeleton composed of calcium carbonate.
(vi) Ctenophores bear eight external rows of ciliated comb plates that help in locomotion.
questions.explanation:
(i) Incorrect: ctenophores reproduce only sexually.
(ii) Correct: in Obelia, medusae form polyps sexually.
(iii) Correct: digestion in cnidarians is both extracellular and intracellular.
(iv) Incorrect: fertilisation in ctenophores is external.
(v) Correct: corals have a calcium carbonate skeleton.
(vi) Correct: ctenophores have eight external rows of ciliated comb plates used for locomotion.
Four statements are correct.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT?
options: In Chondrichthyes, the notochord persists throughout life.
The mouth is ventral in cartilaginous fishes but mostly terminal in bony fishes.
Cyclostomes have a cartilaginous cranium but a bony vertebral column.
Bony fishes have four pairs of gills covered by an operculum on each side.
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: in Chondrichthyes the notochord persists throughout life.
(2) Correct: the mouth is ventral in sharks and rays and mostly terminal in bony fishes.
(3) Incorrect: in cyclostomes both the cranium and the vertebral column are cartilaginous. Neither is bony.
(4) Correct: bony fishes have four pairs of gills, covered by an operculum on each side.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Sponges show a cellular level of organisation, with cells arranged as loose aggregates.
Statement II: Digestion in sponges is extracellular and takes place in the spongocoel.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is true. Sponges are primitive multicellular animals with a cellular level of organisation, and their cells form loose aggregates without true tissues.
Statement II is false. Digestion in sponges is intracellular, carried out inside cells such as choanocytes. The spongocoel is only a water-filled cavity.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In cartilaginous fishes such as Scoliodon, the teeth are:
options: absent, since the mouth is suctorial
questions.explanation:
In Chondrichthyes the skin bears tiny placoid scales.
The teeth are modified placoid scales and point backward, which helps grip prey.
Option (1) fails because cycloid scales belong to bony fishes.
Option (4) fails because a suctorial, jawless mouth is a cyclostome feature. Cartilaginous fishes have strong jaws.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The water vascular system of echinoderms performs all of the following functions EXCEPT:
questions.explanation:
Key fact (NCERT): echinoderms have a water vascular system that helps in locomotion, capture and transport of food, and respiration.
Echinoderms have no excretory system at all. So excretion cannot be a function of the water vascular system.
Respiration may look like the odd one out, but NCERT does list it as a function of this system.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: How many pairs of gill slits for respiration are present on the elongated body of a cyclostome?
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: cyclostomes have an elongated body with 6–15 pairs of gill slits for respiration.
The gill slits open separately to the outside and have no operculum.
The tempting option (2), four pairs of gills covered by an operculum, describes bony fishes (Osteichthyes), not cyclostomes.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In flatworms such as Planaria and Fasciola, specialised cells called flame cells are mainly concerned with:
options: Absorption of nutrients from the host
questions.explanation:
Key NCERT fact: flame cells are specialised cells in Platyhelminthes that help in osmoregulation and excretion.
This matches option (2).
(1) is wrong because parasitic flatworms absorb nutrients directly through their body surface, not through flame cells.
(3) is wrong because attachment to the host is done by hooks and suckers.
(4) is tempting because Planaria has high regeneration capacity. However, regeneration is a property of the whole animal, not the job of flame cells.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following annelids is monoecious, meaning a single individual produces both eggs and sperms?
questions.explanation:
In annelids, earthworms (Pheretima) and leeches are monoecious: one individual produces both eggs and sperms.
Nereis is an aquatic annelid with separate sexes (dioecious), so it is the tempting wrong choice.
Ascaris (aschelminth) and Asterias (echinoderm) are not annelids, and both are dioecious.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following bony fishes is marine?
questions.explanation:
NCERT lists Exocoetus (flying fish) and Hippocampus (sea horse) as marine bony fishes.
Labeo (Rohu), Catla (Katla) and Clarias (Magur) are freshwater bony fishes.
So only Exocoetus is marine.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
(A) Radial symmetry, diploblastic
(B) Bilateral symmetry, acoelomate
(C) Bilateral symmetry, pseudocoelomate
(D) Bilateral symmetry, metamerically segmented coelomate
List-II
(I) Wuchereria
(II) Hirudinaria
(III) Pleurobrachia
(IV) Taenia
questions.explanation:
A: Pleurobrachia is a ctenophore, so it is radial and diploblastic (A-III).
B: Taenia is a flatworm, so it is bilateral and acoelomate (B-IV).
C: Wuchereria is a roundworm, so it is bilateral and pseudocoelomate (C-I).
D: Hirudinaria is an annelid, so it is metamerically segmented and coelomate (D-II).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The digestive tract of birds has two additional chambers. These are:
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: the digestive tract of birds has two additional chambers, the crop and the gizzard.
The crop stores food, and the muscular gizzard grinds it.
Rumen and reticulum are stomach chambers of ruminant mammals, so (2) is wrong.
Air sacs are respiratory structures, and the cloaca is a common opening rather than an additional chamber. This rules out (3) and (4).
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In which of the following animals is an undifferentiated layer, the mesoglea, present between the ectoderm and the endoderm?
questions.explanation:
Diploblastic animals have an undifferentiated mesoglea between the ectoderm and the endoderm.
Hydra is a coelenterate, and coelenterates are diploblastic, so Hydra has mesoglea.
Planaria (flatworm), Ascaris (roundworm) and Pheretima (annelid) are triploblastic. They have a true mesoderm instead of mesoglea.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In cnidarians, the single opening of the central gastro-vascular cavity, the mouth, is located on the:
questions.explanation:
Key fact: cnidarians show extracellular and intracellular digestion in a central gastro-vascular cavity. This cavity has a single opening, the mouth, which lies on the hypostome.
The osculum is the water outlet of sponges, which is why it is a tempting choice.
Proboscis and collar are body regions of hemichordates such as Balanoglossus.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Given below are types of cells present in some animals. Which of the following cells can differentiate to perform different functions?
questions.explanation:
Key fact: Cnidarians such as Hydra have interstitial cells. These are small, undifferentiated cells that act like stem cells.
Interstitial cells can develop into other cell types, including cnidoblasts (stinging cells), nerve cells and gametes.
Choanocytes (collar cells of sponges), gastrodermal cells and nematocytes are already specialised for one job: water current and food capture, digestion, and stinging. They cannot change into other cells.
The tempting choice is nematocytes, but these are themselves formed from interstitial cells.
Answer: (2)
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 4 (MCQ Q2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which arthropod is cited in NCERT as a 'living fossil'?
questions.explanation:
Key NCERT fact: NCERT lists Limulus (king crab) as a living fossil among arthropods.
This matches option (4).
The other options are arthropods described for different reasons:
- Locusta is a gregarious pest.
- Laccifer (lac insect) and Bombyx (silkworm) are economically important insects.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following animals are coelomates?
Ascaris, Pheretima, Pila, Taenia, Asterias, Balanoglossus, Wuchereria
questions.explanation:
Coelomates: Pheretima (annelid), Pila (mollusc), Asterias (echinoderm) and Balanoglossus (hemichordate).
Pseudocoelomates: Ascaris and Wuchereria (aschelminthes).
Acoelomate: Taenia (platyhelminth).
So the number of coelomates is 4.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Cyclostomes are marine but migrate to fresh water for spawning.
Statement II: After spawning, adult cyclostomes migrate back to the ocean.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct: cyclostomes live in the sea and migrate to fresh water to spawn.
Statement II is incorrect: adult cyclostomes die within a few days after spawning.
It is their larvae that return to the ocean after metamorphosis.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following animals belong to class Reptilia?
Chelone, Bufo, Testudo, Salamandra, Vipera, Hyla, Hemidactylus, Ichthyophis
questions.explanation:
Reptiles in the list: Chelone (turtle), Testudo (tortoise), Vipera (viper) and Hemidactylus (wall lizard). That makes 4.
Amphibians in the list: Bufo (toad), Salamandra (salamander), Hyla (tree frog) and Ichthyophis (limbless amphibian).
Two traps to avoid: the lizard-like Salamandra and the snake-like Ichthyophis are both amphibians, not reptiles.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding levels of organisation is incorrect?
options: Ctenophores exhibit the tissue level of organisation
Roundworms (Aschelminthes) exhibit the organ-system level of organisation
In flatworms, tissues are grouped to form organs specialised for particular functions
Cells of sponges show no division of labour at all
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: ctenophores, like cnidarians, show the tissue level of organisation.
(2) Correct: NCERT describes Aschelminthes as having an organ-system level of body organisation.
(3) Correct: in flatworms, tissues are grouped into organs, which is the organ level.
(4) Incorrect: sponge cells form loose aggregates, but NCERT notes that some division of labour does occur among them.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following features are common to BOTH Chondrichthyes and Osteichthyes?
Two-chambered heart; operculum covering the gills; air bladder; poikilothermy; separate sexes; placoid scales; streamlined body; usually external fertilisation
questions.explanation:
Two-chambered heart: common to both classes.
Poikilothermy (cold-blooded): common.
Separate sexes: common.
Streamlined body: common.
Operculum and air bladder: found only in bony fishes (Osteichthyes).
Usually external fertilisation: only bony fishes. Cartilaginous fishes show internal fertilisation.
Placoid scales: only cartilaginous fishes (Chondrichthyes).
So 4 features are shared.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following features is present in Osteichthyes but absent in Chondrichthyes?
questions.explanation:
Osteichthyes (bony fishes) have four pairs of gills covered on each side by an operculum.
Chondrichthyes (cartilaginous fishes) have separate, uncovered gill slits.
Both classes have a two-chambered heart, are cold-blooded (poikilothermous) and have separate sexes. Only the operculum separates them here.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following echinoderms is correctly matched with its common name?
questions.explanation:
NCERT gives these echinoderm examples with their common names: Asterias (star fish), Echinus (sea urchin), Antedon (sea lily), Cucumaria (sea cucumber) and Ophiura (brittle star).
(1) Correct: Antedon is the sea lily.
(2) Wrong: Cucumaria is the sea cucumber, not the brittle star.
(3) Wrong: Ophiura is the brittle star, not the sea urchin.
(4) Wrong: Echinus is the sea urchin. The star fish is Asterias.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following phyla consists of animals in which males and females are distinct individuals (dioecious)?
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that Aschelminthes (roundworms) are dioecious. Males and females are separate individuals, and the females are often longer than the males.
Porifera (sponges), Ctenophora and Platyhelminthes are all described as hermaphrodite, so both sexes occur in the same individual.
This makes Aschelminthes the only dioecious phylum among the options.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following features are shared by both Taenia (tapeworm) and Ascaris (roundworm)?
(i) Bilateral symmetry
(ii) Triploblastic body organisation
(iii) Internal fertilisation
(iv) Complete alimentary canal
(v) Separate sexes (dioecious condition)
(vi) Excretion through flame cells
(vii) Presence of a body cavity
questions.explanation:
Check each feature for Taenia and Ascaris:
(i) Shared: both are bilaterally symmetrical.
(ii) Shared: both are triploblastic.
(iii) Shared: fertilisation is internal in both.
(iv) Not shared: Taenia has no complete gut; only Ascaris does.
(v) Not shared: Taenia is hermaphrodite, while Ascaris is dioecious.
(vi) Not shared: only flatworms such as Taenia have flame cells.
(vii) Not shared: Taenia is acoelomate, while Ascaris has a pseudocoelom.
That gives 3 shared features.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
A. Pristis
B. Betta
C. Myxine
D. Pterophyllum
List-II
(i) Angel fish
(ii) Hagfish
(iii) Saw fish
(iv) Fighting fish
questions.explanation:
A. Pristis is the saw fish (iii).
B. Betta is the fighting fish (iv).
C. Myxine is the hagfish (ii), a cyclostome.
D. Pterophyllum is the angel fish (i).
Betta and Pterophyllum are both aquarium fishes, so do not swap them.
The matching is A-iii, B-iv, C-ii, D-i.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the mode of fertilisation and type of development?
options: Osteichthyes: fertilisation usually external, development indirect
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: NCERT states sponges show internal fertilisation and indirect development, with a larval stage morphologically distinct from the adult.
(2) Incorrect: ctenophores have external fertilisation and indirect development, not internal and direct.
(3) Incorrect: in bony fishes fertilisation is usually external, but they are mostly oviparous and development is direct. This is the most tempting wrong option, since its first half is true.
(4) Incorrect: echinoderms show external fertilisation and indirect development through a free-swimming larva.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The division Agnatha of subphylum Vertebrata is represented by the class:
questions.explanation:
Subphylum Vertebrata is divided into Agnatha (no jaws) and Gnathostomata (with jaws).
Agnatha contains only one class, Cyclostomata, e.g., Petromyzon (lamprey) and Myxine (hagfish).
Chondrichthyes, Osteichthyes and Amphibia all have jaws, so they belong to Gnathostomata.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In which of the following groups are cells that perform the same function first arranged into tissues, giving a tissue level of organisation?
questions.explanation:
Coelenterates are the first group in which cells performing the same function are grouped into tissues. This is the tissue level of organisation.
Sponges (Porifera) have only loose cell aggregates, which is the cellular level.
Platyhelminthes reach the organ level.
Annelids reach the organ-system level.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Both cnidarians and ctenophores show extracellular as well as intracellular digestion
Ctenophores reproduce only sexually, with external fertilisation and indirect development
In Obelia, medusae produce polyps asexually and polyps produce medusae sexually
Sponges are hermaphrodite with internal fertilisation and a larval stage distinct from the adult
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct. Both groups digest food in the gastrovascular cavity (extracellular) and inside cells (intracellular).
(2) Correct. Ctenophores reproduce only sexually, with external fertilisation and indirect development.
(3) Incorrect. In Obelia (metagenesis), polyps produce medusae asexually, and medusae form polyps sexually. The statement reverses this.
(4) Correct. Sponges are hermaphrodite, fertilisation is internal, and development is indirect, with a larva distinct from the adult.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The skin of birds is dry and lacks glands, with one exception. Which gland is present in the skin of birds?
options: Sweat gland on the hind limbs
Oil gland at the base of the tail
Mammary gland on the ventral side
Mucous gland all over the body
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that bird skin is dry and has no glands except the oil (preen) gland at the base of the tail.
The bird uses this oil to keep its feathers in good condition, so (2) fits.
Mammary and sweat glands are mammalian features, which rules out (1) and (3).
Mucous glands in moist skin are typical of amphibians, which rules out (4).
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Pheretima (earthworm) and Hirudinaria (leech) are monoecious annelids.
Reason (R): Nereis, an aquatic annelid, has separate male and female individuals.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: Pheretima (earthworm) and Hirudinaria (leech) are monoecious, meaning each individual is a hermaphrodite.
R is true: Nereis is dioecious, with separate male and female individuals.
R is not the correct explanation of A. The sexual condition of Nereis says nothing about why earthworms and leeches are hermaphrodites. NCERT simply lists both conditions as variations within Annelida.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In which of the following groups can the body be divided into identical left and right halves in only one plane?
questions.explanation:
If a body can be cut into identical left and right halves in only one plane, it is bilaterally symmetrical.
Annelids such as the earthworm are bilaterally symmetrical, so option (4) fits.
Coelenterates and ctenophores are radially symmetrical. Any plane through their central axis gives identical halves, so they have more than one such plane.
Sponges are mostly asymmetrical.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Reptiles usually have a three-chambered heart. Which of the following reptiles is an exception with a four-chambered heart?
questions.explanation:
NCERT notes that the reptilian heart is usually three-chambered, with two auricles and one ventricle.
Crocodiles (Crocodilus) are the exception, with a four-chambered heart.
Chelone (turtle), Calotes (garden lizard) and Naja (cobra) all have the usual three-chambered heart.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In some animals the body cavity is not lined by mesoderm; instead, the mesoderm lies as scattered pouches between the ectoderm and endoderm. Which animal shows this type of body cavity?
questions.explanation:
A pseudocoelom forms when mesoderm lies as scattered pouches between ectoderm and endoderm and does not line the body cavity.
NCERT gives Aschelminthes (roundworms) as the example, and Ascaris is a roundworm, so it fits.
Fasciola (a flatworm) is acoelomate, with no body cavity at all.
Nereis (annelid) and Balanoglossus (hemichordate) have a true coelom lined by mesoderm.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Locomotion in Pleurobrachia is brought about by:
options: Eight external rows of ciliated comb plates
questions.explanation:
Key fact: Pleurobrachia is a ctenophore (comb jelly).
Its body bears eight external rows of ciliated comb plates, and these help in locomotion.
Parapodia are the swimming appendages of Nereis, an annelid. The water vascular system belongs to echinoderms.
The tempting option is tentacles with cnidoblasts. Ctenophores lack cnidoblasts, and tentacles are not used for locomotion.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The notochord, which separates chordates from non-chordates, is best described as a rod-like structure that is:
options: Ectodermally derived and formed on the dorsal side during embryonic development
Mesodermally derived and formed on the dorsal side during embryonic development
Mesodermally derived and formed on the ventral side during embryonic development
Endodermally derived and formed on the ventral side of the gut
questions.explanation:
The notochord is a rod-like structure that only chordates have.
NCERT defines it as derived from mesoderm and formed on the dorsal side of the embryo.
Option (1) is the tempting trap. It describes the dorsal hollow nerve cord, which is ectodermal, not the notochord.
Options (3) and (4) are wrong because the notochord is dorsal, not ventral. It is also not endodermal.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
A small, exclusively marine animal has the following features:
- a dorsal hollow nerve cord
- paired pharyngeal gill slits
- a notochord that extends from head to tail and persists throughout life
- no vertebral column at any stage
The animal is most likely:
questions.explanation:
A notochord running from head to tail and persisting throughout life, with no vertebral column at any stage, marks Cephalochordata. Branchiostoma (Amphioxus) is the example.
Ascidia is a urochordate, so its notochord is found only in the larval tail.
Petromyzon is a vertebrate (cyclostome) and has a vertebral column.
Balanoglossus is a hemichordate. It has only a stomochord, not a true notochord.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following features are common to both Aves and Mammalia?
Four-chambered heart; homoiothermy; internal fertilisation; direct development; respiration by lungs; external pinnae; feathers; oil gland at the base of the tail
questions.explanation:
Four-chambered heart: present in both classes.
Homoiothermy: present in both.
Internal fertilisation: occurs in both.
Direct development: NCERT states this for both birds and mammals.
Respiration by lungs: occurs in both.
External pinnae: found only in mammals.
Feathers and the oil gland at the base of the tail: found only in birds.
That gives 5 shared features.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following sets of animals belong to a single taxonomic group?
questions.explanation:
Monkey, chimpanzee and man are all mammals of the order Primates, so they form a single taxonomic group.
Option (1) is mixed: cuttlefish (Mollusca), jellyfish (Cnidaria), silverfish (Arthropoda), dogfish (fish) and starfish (Echinodermata).
Option (2) is mixed: bat (Mammalia), pigeon (Aves) and butterfly (Insecta).
Option (4) is mixed: silkworm (Arthropoda), tapeworm (Platyhelminthes) and earthworm (Annelida).
Answer: (3)
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 4 (MCQ Q6)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are true for members of Phylum Porifera?
(i) They are generally marine.
(ii) They are mostly asymmetrical.
(iii) Digestion is extracellular.
(iv) Sexes are separate.
(v) They reproduce asexually by fragmentation.
(vi) Fertilisation is external.
questions.explanation:
(i) True: sponges are generally marine.
(ii) True: they are mostly asymmetrical.
(iii) False: digestion is intracellular.
(iv) False: sexes are not separate, because sponges are hermaphrodite.
(v) True: they reproduce asexually by fragmentation.
(vi) False: fertilisation is internal.
Three statements are true.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about Class Amphibia and Class Reptilia are correct?
(i) In both classes, the ear is represented by a tympanum.
(ii) Fertilisation is external in both classes.
(iii) Crocodilus has a four-chambered heart, whereas Rana has a three-chambered heart.
(iv) Both classes are oviparous with indirect development.
(v) Ichthyophis is a limbless reptile.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: in both amphibians and reptiles, the ear is represented by a tympanum.
(ii) Wrong: reptiles have internal fertilisation.
(iii) Correct: Crocodilus has a four-chambered heart and Rana a three-chambered heart.
(iv) Wrong: reptiles show direct development.
(v) Wrong: Ichthyophis is a limbless amphibian.
So two statements are correct.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following animals have an open circulatory system?
Prawn, Balanoglossus, Nereis, Petromyzon, Scorpion
questions.explanation:
Prawn: arthropod, so open circulation. Yes.
Balanoglossus: hemichordate, so open circulation. Yes.
Nereis: annelid, so closed circulation. No.
Petromyzon: cyclostome (a chordate), so closed circulation. No.
Scorpion: arthropod, so open circulation. Yes.
Three animals have an open circulatory system.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A marine animal has the following features: it is triploblastic and coelomate, its body is unsegmented, its digestive tract is complete, it has no excretory system, and its larva is bilaterally symmetrical while the adult is radially symmetrical. This animal is most likely:
questions.explanation:
Two clues point to Echinodermata: there is no excretory system, and the adult is radial while the larva is bilateral.
Ophiura (brittle star) is an echinoderm, so it fits.
Balanoglossus is a hemichordate with a proboscis gland for excretion.
Chaetopleura and Loligo are bilaterally symmetrical molluscs whose gills also help in excretion.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following is oviparous?
questions.explanation:
Key fact: Most mammals are viviparous. Prototherians (monotremes) such as the platypus are the exception, because they lay eggs (oviparous).
The flying fox (bat), elephant and whale are all viviparous placental mammals.
The whale may be tempting because it lives in water, but it still gives birth to live young.
Answer: (1)
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 4 (MCQ Q9)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which option correctly contrasts Porifera with Coelenterata?
options: Porifera: digestion only intracellular; Coelenterata: digestion both extracellular and intracellular
Porifera: radial symmetry; Coelenterata: mostly asymmetrical
Porifera: tissue level of organisation; Coelenterata: cellular level of organisation
Porifera: mouth on hypostome; Coelenterata: water exits through osculum
questions.explanation:
Porifera digest food only inside cells (intracellular digestion).
Coelenterates digest food both in the gastro-vascular cavity (extracellular) and within cells (intracellular). So option (1) is a correct contrast.
Option (2) is wrong: sponges are mostly asymmetrical and cnidarians are radially symmetrical.
Option (3) is wrong: sponges have cellular-level organisation and cnidarians have tissue-level organisation.
Option (4) is wrong: the hypostome belongs to cnidarians and the osculum belongs to sponges.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: In Cephalochordata, the notochord extends from head to tail and persists throughout life.
Statement II: In Vertebrata, the notochord is present only in the larval tail.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. In cephalochordates such as Branchiostoma, the notochord extends from head to tail and persists throughout life.
Statement II is incorrect. A notochord restricted to the larval tail is a feature of Urochordata. In vertebrates, the notochord is present in the embryo and is replaced by a vertebral column in the adult.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about ctenophores are correct?
(i) They are exclusively marine.
(ii) They are radially symmetrical.
(iii) They are diploblastic.
(iv) They reproduce both asexually and sexually.
(v) Fertilisation is internal.
(vi) Bioluminescence is well-marked.
(vii) Sexes are not separate.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: ctenophores are exclusively marine.
(ii) Correct: they are radially symmetrical.
(iii) Correct: they are diploblastic.
(iv) Incorrect: they reproduce only by sexual means.
(v) Incorrect: fertilisation is external, and development is indirect.
(vi) Correct: bioluminescence is well-marked.
(vii) Correct: sexes are not separate, so they are hermaphrodite.
So five statements are correct.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following features correctly describes members of class Cyclostomata such as Petromyzon?
options: Body covered with minute placoid scales
questions.explanation:
Cyclostomes are jawless vertebrates with a sucking, circular mouth. This matches option (2).
They have no scales, so placoid scales are wrong.
They have no paired fins.
Their cranium and vertebral column are cartilaginous, not bony.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Apis
(b) Bombyx
(c) Laccifer
(d) Locusta
List-II
(i) Gregarious pest
(ii) Lac insect
(iii) Honey bee
(iv) Silkworm
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation:
(a) Apis is the honey bee, so it matches (iii).
(b) Bombyx is the silkworm, so it matches (iv).
(c) Laccifer is the lac insect, so it matches (ii).
(d) Locusta is the gregarious pest, so it matches (i).
The common mistake is swapping Apis and Bombyx, as option (2) does. Remember that Bombyx gives silk.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about phylum Arthropoda is incorrect?
options: The body is covered by a chitinous exoskeleton
More than two-thirds of all named species on earth are arthropods
Blood flows only within a closed network of arteries, veins and capillaries
Members are mostly oviparous and fertilisation is usually internal
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: arthropods have a chitinous exoskeleton.
(2) Correct: arthropods make up over two-thirds of all named species, the largest phylum.
(3) Incorrect: arthropods have an open circulatory system, in which blood flows into spaces and bathes the tissues directly. A closed system of vessels belongs to annelids.
(4) Correct: arthropods are mostly oviparous with usually internal fertilisation.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following is a non-poisonous snake?
questions.explanation:
Key fact: Snakes are either venomous, injecting toxin through fangs, or non-venomous, killing prey another way.
Python: It is non-venomous. It coils around its prey and kills it by constriction (squeezing).
Cobra, viper and krait: All three are poisonous snakes. The tempting option, viper, has prominent venom fangs.
So the only non-poisonous snake listed is the python.
Answer: (3)
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 4 (MCQ Q10)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Read the following statements comparing chordates and non-chordates.
Statement I: In chordates the heart is ventral, whereas in non-chordates the heart, if present, is dorsal.
Statement II: In non-chordates the central nervous system is dorsal, solid and single.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. Chordates have a ventral heart, while non-chordates have a dorsal heart when one is present.
Statement II is incorrect. In non-chordates the CNS is ventral, solid and double. A dorsal, hollow, single CNS is the chordate condition.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): All vertebrates are chordates, but all chordates are not vertebrates.
Reason (R): Urochordates and cephalochordates possess a notochord but never develop a vertebral column.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Every vertebrate has a notochord at the embryonic stage, so every vertebrate is a chordate.
R is true. Urochordates and cephalochordates (the protochordates) have a notochord but never form a vertebral column.
R explains A. These protochordates are the chordates that are not vertebrates, so R accounts for the second half of A.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Read the following statements about Aschelminthes.
Statement I: In roundworms, the body cavity is completely lined by mesoderm.
Statement II: Roundworms are dioecious, and females are often longer than males.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is incorrect. Roundworms are pseudocoelomates. Their mesoderm is present as scattered pouches between the ectoderm and endoderm and does not line the body cavity. A cavity fully lined by mesoderm is a true coelom.
Statement II is correct. Aschelminthes are dioecious, and females are often longer than males.
So Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Read the following statements.
Statement I: Hemichordates possess a true notochord in the collar region and are therefore now placed as a subphylum of Chordata.
Statement II: In Urochordata, the notochord is present only in the larval tail.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is incorrect. Hemichordates have only a stomochord, a rudimentary structure similar to a notochord, not a true notochord. They are now placed as a separate phylum under non-chordata, not as a subphylum of Chordata.
Statement II is correct. In Urochordata, the notochord is present only in the larval tail.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In which of the following animals are cells performing the same function arranged into tissues, but tissues are not grouped into organs?
questions.explanation:
Key fact: The arrangement described, with cells grouped into tissues but tissues not grouped into organs, is the tissue level of organisation. It is seen in coelenterates (cnidarians).
Adamsia (sea anemone) is a coelenterate, so it fits.
Why not the others: Sycon is a sponge at the cellular level. Fasciola is at the organ level, and Pheretima is at the organ-system level.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Ichthyophis is best described as:
questions.explanation:
NCERT lists Ichthyophis as the limbless amphibian of Class Amphibia.
It has moist skin and lays eggs that develop indirectly, like other amphibians. It is not a reptile or a fish.
Its long, legless body makes the snake option tempting. Snakes are reptiles with dry, scaly skin, and Ichthyophis is not poisonous.
It has no fins or gills as an adult, so 'bony fish' is also wrong.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
A. Physalia
B. Adamsia
C. Pennatula
D. Gorgonia
List-II
I. Sea-fan
II. Portuguese man-of-war
III. Sea-pen
IV. Sea anemone
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation:
A. Physalia is the Portuguese man-of-war, so A matches II.
B. Adamsia is the sea anemone, so B matches IV.
C. Pennatula is the sea-pen, so C matches III.
D. Gorgonia is the sea-fan, so D matches I.
This gives A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I.
Answer: (1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Anopheles, Culex and Aedes are arthropods that are best described as:
options: Insects of economic importance producing useful products
questions.explanation:
Key fact (NCERT): Anopheles, Culex and Aedes are mosquitoes listed as vectors. They carry and transmit pathogens such as malaria parasites, filarial worms and dengue virus.
Option (2) fits because NCERT classifies them by this role.
Option (1) fails because the gregarious pest is Locusta.
Option (3) fails because the living fossil is Limulus (king crab).
Option (4) fails because insects giving useful products are Apis, Bombyx and Laccifer.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following correctly contrasts Platyhelminthes with Aschelminthes as described in NCERT?
options: Platyhelminthes have an excretory pore, whereas Aschelminthes excrete through flame cells
Platyhelminthes have an incomplete digestive system and are hermaphrodite, whereas Aschelminthes have a complete alimentary canal and are dioecious
Both phyla possess an open circulatory system but lack respiratory organs
Platyhelminthes are pseudocoelomate, whereas Aschelminthes are acoelomate
questions.explanation:
Key NCERT fact: Platyhelminthes have an incomplete gut with a single opening, and their sexes are not separate (hermaphrodite). Aschelminthes have a complete alimentary canal with a muscular pharynx, and their sexes are separate (dioecious).
Option (2) states exactly this contrast.
(1) is wrong because the structures are swapped. Flame cells belong to flatworms, while roundworms have an excretory pore.
(3) is wrong because neither phylum has a circulatory system.
(4) is wrong because the body cavities are swapped. Flatworms are acoelomate and roundworms are pseudocoelomate.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Hemichordata is now placed as a separate phylum under non-chordata.
Reason (R): Hemichordates have a rudimentary structure called stomochord in the collar region, which is similar to the notochord.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: Hemichordata was earlier a sub-phylum of Chordata but is now a separate phylum under non-chordata.
R is true: hemichordates have a rudimentary stomochord in the collar region, similar to the notochord.
However, the notochord-like stomochord is why they were once grouped with chordates. It does not explain their shift to non-chordata, so R is not the correct explanation of A.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following molluscs is correctly matched with its common name?
questions.explanation:
(1) Wrong: Sepia is the cuttlefish. The squid is Loligo.
(2) Wrong: Dentalium is the tusk shell. The chiton is Chaetopleura.
(3) Correct: Pinctada is the pearl oyster.
(4) Wrong: Aplysia is the sea-hare. The devil fish is Octopus.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Sponges are said to show a cellular level of organisation because:
options: Their cells performing the same function are grouped into tissues
Their cells are arranged as loose cell aggregates
Their tissues are grouped to form organs
Their organs are associated to form organ systems
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: in the cellular level of organisation, cells are arranged as loose aggregates.
Sponges show this level. Their cells share some division of labour but do not form true tissues.
Option (1), cells grouped into tissues, describes the tissue level. This first appears in coelenterates.
Options (3) and (4) describe the organ and organ-system levels, which are found in higher animals.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is a freshwater sponge?
questions.explanation:
NCERT gives Spongilla as the example of a freshwater sponge.
Sycon (also called Scypha) is a marine sponge.
Euspongia is the marine bath sponge.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: External ears, or pinnae, are a characteristic feature of which of the following classes?
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: mammals have external ears, called pinnae.
In amphibians, a tympanum represents the ear.
Reptiles also have a tympanum, but they have no external ear openings.
Birds have ear openings but no pinnae.
So pinnae are characteristic of class Mammalia only.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A student examines a transverse section of a worm. The section is circular in outline. A body cavity lies between the body wall and the gut, but mesoderm does not line this cavity and is seen only as scattered patches. A muscular pharynx is visible in a section taken near the anterior end, and male and female individuals are found separately. The worm is most likely:
questions.explanation:
The worm shows four key features: a circular cross-section, a cavity not lined by mesoderm (a pseudocoelom), a muscular pharynx and separate sexes. Together these point to Aschelminthes.
Ancylostoma (hookworm) is a roundworm, so it fits every feature.
Fasciola and Planaria are dorsoventrally flattened acoelomates.
Nereis is an annelid with a true coelom lined by mesoderm, so it does not fit.
Answer: (4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following animals are oviparous and show direct development?
Calotes, Columba, Rana, Pila, Catla, Ornithorhynchus, Hyla
questions.explanation:
Oviparous with direct development:
- Calotes (reptile)
- Columba (bird)
- Catla (bony fish)
- Ornithorhynchus (egg-laying mammal)
Indirect development:
- Rana and Hyla (amphibians, which have a tadpole larva)
- Pila (mollusc, with larval development)
So the count is 4.
Answer: (2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following coelenterates is commonly called the brain coral?
questions.explanation:
Key fact: NCERT names Meandrina as the brain coral.
The other options are also cnidarians, which makes them tempting:
- Pennatula is the sea-pen.
- Gorgonia is the sea-fan.
- Physalia is the Portuguese man-of-war.
Answer: (3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 4 · Animal Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (level of organisation) with List-II (animal):
List-I
A. Cellular level
B. Tissue level
C. Organ level
D. Organ-system level
List-II
I. Taenia
II. Pila
III. Spongilla
IV. Pleurobrachia
questions.explanation:
A. Cellular level: Spongilla is a sponge. Its cells form only loose aggregates (III).
B. Tissue level: Pleurobrachia is a ctenophore. Its cells are organised into tissues but not into organs (IV).
C. Organ level: Taenia is a flatworm. Its tissues are grouped into organs (I).
D. Organ-system level: Pila is a mollusc. Its organs work together as systems (II).
The tempting option (4) swaps C and D. Flatworms do not reach the organ-system level.
Answer: (1)
